extracted.intended_audience: independent external experts (reviewers) evaluating ERC Proof of Concept (PoC) Grant proposals
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for independent external experts performing remote and (if needed) panel evaluations of ERC Proof of Concept grant proposals under the ERC Work Programme 2026, including marks, required comments, conflict-of-interest and confidentiality rules, resource assessment and ranking procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sole evaluation criterion of excellence (three elements)
rubrics_metrics.description: The sole evaluation criterion of excellence consists of the following evaluation elements: Project 1.a Breakthrough innovation potential; 1.b Approach and methodology; Principal Investigator 1.c Strategic lead and project management. All judgement on proposals must be made against the evaluation elements and against these evaluation elements alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experts must use only these evaluation elements to assess proposals. The incorrect application of an evaluation element or the application of an inexistent or irrelevant evaluation element is considered a procedural error and may justify re-evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion 1.a — Breakthrough innovation potential
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the proposed idea have the potential to drive innovation and business inventiveness and/or tackle societal challenges? Are the proposed expected outcomes innovative or distinctive compared to existing solutions? Is the proposed idea high risk–high gain? If successful, will the outcome result in a breakthrough innovation? Is there a risk that some aspects are difficult to overcome?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the idea could lead to breakthrough outcomes and weigh potential impact and novelty versus technical/business/societal landscape; identify key risks and whether they are intrinsic to the high-risk/high-gain nature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion 1.b — Approach and methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the proposed activities and planning appropriate and effective to explore the pathway from ground-breaking research towards innovation? Activities may include testing, experimenting, demonstrating and validating the idea; conducting research required to address weaknesses uncovered; clarifying IPR protection or knowledge transfer strategy; involving industry, societal organisations, policymakers or other stakeholders; assessing potential end users. Are the proposed timescales and resources adequate and properly justified? Will activities be conducted by persons well qualified for the purpose?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the suitability and feasibility of activities and timelines. Pay particular attention to the narrative justification of timescales and resources (see 'Resources assessment' guidance). Do not assess budget figures; focus on adequacy and justification of resources and the plan to progress from research to innovation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion 1.c — Principal Investigator: strategic lead and project management
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the PI demonstrate a clear vision on how to manage the project, the consolidation of information and data needed to take strategic decisions and implement the proposed plan, including risk and contingency measures?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge the PI's capability to lead and manage the PoC activities strategically, including risk management and decision-making processes. Avoid comments about the PI's host institution (not an ERC evaluation criterion) and avoid personal characteristics unrelated to project leadership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marks per element and pass/fail requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Independent external experts will evaluate each admissible and eligible proposal and mark it as 'very good', 'good' or 'fail' for each of the three evaluation elements. In order to be considered for funding, proposals will have to be awarded a pass mark ('very good' or 'good') by a majority of independent external experts on each of the three evaluation elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each element is judged separately; a proposal that fails one or more elements will not be ranked or funded. Ensure marks are consistent with explanatory comments. Only the three elements may be used as criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual review minimum requirements and lead reviewer role
rubrics_metrics.description: Each proposal is evaluated by at least 3 experts. If a panel meeting takes place, each proposal is assigned to a 'lead reviewer' who introduces the proposal to the panel and is responsible for drafting the panel comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete individual remote reviews by the deadline. If you lack sufficient expertise for a proposal, inform the ERCEA PoC call coordinator immediately so it can be reallocated. During remote review there must be no discussions between experts about proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality standards for individual reviewers' comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual comments should be high quality, genuine, succinct but substantial, and polite. Provide a succinct explanatory comment substantiating each mark — statement and explanation of key strengths and key weaknesses in light of the evaluation elements. A 'fail' must be explained in detail; a 'good' should explain why not 'very good'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe the following: provide substantial, explanatory comments (avoid mere description or summary); use dispassionate, analytical and unambiguous language; use grammatically correct, complete, clear sentences with no jargon; be respectful and constructive; avoid self-declaration of insufficient expertise; avoid any comments revealing your identity; do not reference applicant’s age, nationality, gender, or personal matters; avoid references to marks in comments; avoid inconsistency between comment and mark; be aware of unconscious bias (gender and diversity); avoid comments on PI’s host institution; avoid comparisons with other proposals or previous assessments; avoid dismissive statements; avoid very short comments especially for 'fail'; double-check submitted marks correspond to intended marks; avoid comments on ethics and security (handled separately); avoid references to costs/budget figures when assessing resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts of interest (CoI) — list and declaration responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Experts should not be put in a situation in which their impartiality might be questioned. A list of conflicts of interests is displayed in the online evaluation system and experts must confirm absence of CoI when accepting to review and when submitting their individual review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples (non-exhaustive) include: I am PI or team member in the proposal; I was involved in preparation of the proposal; I would benefit from the proposal's acceptance/rejection; I am employed/contracted by an entity involved (past 3 years); I am a director/trustee/partner in an entity involved (past 3 years); I collaborated scientifically with the PI (past 5 years); I have mentor/mentee relationship with the PI; family/close personal relationship with PI or persons involved; relationship of scientific rivalry/hostility with the PI; I am a National Contact Point or work for Enterprise Europe Network; I am member of an EU programme committee; or any other situation precluding impartiality. It is the expert's responsibility to declare CoIs; the ERCEA will try to avoid assigning proposals if CoI is present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality and use of personal data
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should not engage in any contact with applicants or beneficiaries about the evaluation, during or after the evaluation. Personal data are to be used only for the purposes for which they are transmitted. Unnecessary and excessive information submitted by applicants should be disregarded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not disclose proposals assigned for your evaluation to other experts. Panel member names are published after evaluation is concluded. Maintain confidentiality obligations from the expert contract and Code of Conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admissibility and eligibility — ERCEA responsibility; expert flagging
rubrics_metrics.description: Admissibility and eligibility criteria are simple, factual and legally binding and are assessed by ERCEA staff; they do not involve technical or scientific judgement and are not part of the review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an expert considers a proposal potentially inadmissible or ineligible (e.g., incomplete sections), they should clarify immediately with the ERC PoC call coordinator. Proposals may be declared inadmissible/ineligible during or after evaluation if criteria are not met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resources assessment and lump sum guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: PoC grants take the form of a standard lump sum pre-fixed at EUR 150,000 for a period of eighteen months (lump sum deemed to cover all eligible costs). The Principal Investigator must demonstrate that proposed timescales and resources are adequate and properly justified (part of element 1.b). Applicants should provide a narrative description of resources planned for each activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessors should examine whether timescales and resource descriptions (type of staff and estimated effort, equipment, consumables, travel, etc.) are adequate and justified. Applicants are specifically requested not to describe resources financially (no cost figures). If budget figures appear, experts shall disregard them and must not penalise the applicant. If insufficient detail on resources is provided, experts may comment on this deficiency (but should avoid referring to costs/budget figures).

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of support or intent handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Experts have access to annexes containing Letters of support or intent from relevant stakeholders. Applicants are asked to include such contacts to document section 1b.ii - description of PoC activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letters of support are available for reviewers to assess stated stakeholder engagement. Annexes do not count towards Part B page limit (10 pages).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics and Security handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Experts should disregard any Ethics and Security issues annexes, as Ethical clearance is performed by ERCEA and Security clearance by the European Commission for all proposals selected for funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid comments on ethical and security aspects except: flag and report any use of human embryonic stem cells (hESC) to the ERC PoC call coordinator; if hESC are involved, confirm whether their use is necessary to achieve objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial Panel Meeting briefing and agreement to methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: At the start of the evaluation session experts are invited to the Initial Panel Meeting to be briefed on evaluation processes/procedures and to exchange views with ERCEA staff. ERCEA staff presents the methodology for evaluation, marking and final ranking, and experts agree to follow a remote evaluation process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experts are strongly encouraged to participate. At the Initial Panel Meeting experts explicitly agree and this is minuted. If agreement is not reached, a final ranking meeting is offered. Tie-breaking methodology is agreed ahead of time if remote evaluation is used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remote review and ranking procedures, sorting order
rubrics_metrics.description: Each proposal evaluated remotely by at least 3 experts. If budget insufficient, proposals that pass all three elements will be ranked according to aggregated marks sorted by: i) evaluation element 1.a Breakthrough innovation potential; ii) element 1.b Approach and methodology; iii) element 1.c Principal Investigator - Strategic lead and project management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fund proposals in order of the 3-level sorting until available budget is exhausted. If ties arise, experts may meet as a panel to determine priority or follow the pre-agreed tie-breaking method. Proposals recommended for funding without sufficient funds may be put on a reserve list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voting and tie-resolution within groups of equally ranked proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: The panel may finalise ranking using a voting system (majority vote). If a group of equally ranked fundable proposals crosses the budget cut-off, the process is: circulate reviews of group to relevant experts (taking CoIs into account, anonymously), experts examine proposals and existing reviews and decide personal rankings, ERCEA compiles a sub-ranking accounting for CoIs and produces overall final ranking for endorsement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An expert cannot vote for a proposal if under a CoI; appropriate adjustments applied. Voting is an effective way to finalise a ranking list. Remote procedures are used wherever possible; panel meetings held only if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel report content
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to the ranked list of proposals, the panel report briefly documents the evaluation methodology followed by the panel. It may contain reflections on issues such as the quality of proposals in relation to the call budget and other observations or recommendations for future evaluations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panel report complements the ranked list and may inform ERC Scientific Council of procedural or quality observations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feedback to applicants — Evaluation Report composition and editing rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The Evaluation Report documents results and is composed of: (i) the recommendation of the panel (according to ranking and available budget); (ii) the ranking range of the proposal among all proposals evaluated by the panel; and (iii) a compilation of the individual reviews by evaluation element including the final marks for each element ('pass' or 'fail').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments by experts are included as received. ERCEA will not change content except to improve readability or, exceptionally, remove clerical errors or inappropriate comments provided such edits do not affect evaluation results. Individual comments may legitimately diverge; ERCEA may contact experts for clarification if potential irregularities are spotted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of electronic tools (SEP) for evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: During remote evaluation experts work individually using the online Submission and Evaluation of Proposals System (SEP).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quick guides, detailed procedures and instructional videos on SEP are available; experts should follow the SEP workflow (confirm CoI, submit marks/comments, approve panel ranking electronically).
